## Send daily AI-summarized competitor content digests to Slack and email via ScraperAPI

### How it works

1. Triggers start the workflow manually or automatically on a schedule.
2. Initialization nodes prepare data tables for storing and comparing snapshots.
3. Crawling nodes set and initiate web scraping through configured URLs.
4. Webhook nodes receive and parse scrape data for further analysis.
5. Processing nodes compare the scraped content with historical snapshots.
6. Conditional nodes determine if content changes are significant and proceed accordingly.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure credentials for ScraperAPI to enable web crawling.
- [ ] Set up webhook URLs to listen for crawl results.
- [ ] Input competitor start URLs in the Configure URLs node.
- [ ] Set up Slack API credentials for posting digests.

### Customization

Users can customize the competitor start URLs to monitor different websites or sections.

## Manual start workflow

Initializes the workflow interactively

## Scheduled crawl trigger

Starts the crawl process on a schedule

## Receive crawl results

Handles incoming scraped data

## Content comparison

Compares new crawled data with previous snapshots

## Handle content updates

Processes changes using AI and archives data

## Daily digest workflow

Compiles and sends daily summaries of changes

## Broadcast daily digest

Sends compiled updates via various channels

## AI summarization

Uses AI to summarize content changes

options.systemMessage: You are a competitive intelligence analyst. You receive snapshots of competitor web pages and produce short, factual summaries of what has changed since the previous snapshot. Be specific and concise. Cite concrete details (product names, prices, dates) when present.
